posts.lexical:
{"root":{"children":[{"type":"html","version":1,"html":"

Evidence hierarchy

Every source is classed A–F. The class decides how we may describe what it shows. An FIR proves a case was registered — not that the accused committed the offence.

A

Final judicial finding

Final judgment, conviction or acquittal, final appellate outcome.

How we describe it: State the precise finding, date, issues decided and appeal status.

B

Official adjudicatory or audit finding

RERA order, tribunal order, audit observation, departmental finding.

How we describe it: Attribute to the authority and quote within its scope. An audit observation is not a conviction.

C

Formal investigative record

FIR, trap case, chargesheet, prosecution complaint, attachment order.

How we describe it: Say “registered”, “filed”, “alleged” or “attached”. State whether investigation or trial is pending.

D

Primary private record

Agreement, receipt, correspondence, bank statement, survey material.

How we describe it: Authenticate origin, context and completeness. Redact third-party personal data.

E

First-hand testimony

Buyer, witness, former employee or resident interview.

How we describe it: Attribute carefully, assess basis of knowledge, corroborate independently.

F

Secondary reporting

News stories, social posts, public videos.

How we describe it: A lead or attributed account only — never the sole basis for a serious allegation.

"},{"type":"html","version":1,"html":"

Status labels

The status on a record describes the procedural stage reached — nothing more.

  1. Complaint received

    A complaint was filed with an identifiable body. A complaint does not establish the claim.

  2. FIR / investigation

    Police or an agency registered or is investigating the allegation. No finding has been made.

  3. Charges filed

    The agency has filed a chargesheet or prosecution complaint. The trial outcome is pending.

  4. Regulatory / audit finding

    A regulator, tribunal, auditor or department made a specific finding, attributed here within its scope.

  5. Trial / proceeding pending

    A court or tribunal proceeding is still active. See the last-checked date.

  6. Judgment / order issued

    A court or tribunal decided specific issues. The operative finding is summarised, not one side's argument.

  7. Appeal / review pending

    An appeal, review or stay is pending. The earlier outcome is not final.

  8. Closed / final outcome

    The proceeding is closed. The exact outcome and any remaining appeal route are stated.

"},{"type":"html","version":1,"html":"

Ten-step research workflow

AI tools may assist with extraction and drafting under human review. They never decide guilt, status or publication.

  1. Lead discovery

    Candidate leads come from official portals, court records, audit reports, news archives and citizen tips. A lead gets an internal ID and is never published at this stage.

  2. Lead triage

    We assess public-interest value, relevance to the states and period, potential harm, source reliability, duplication and legal risk.

  3. Record acquisition

    Official downloads, certified copies, RTI responses, filings, agreements and interviews — with acquisition date and method logged.

  4. Preservation

    The original is stored read-only with a SHA-256 hash and source reference. Work happens on a copy.

  5. Claim decomposition

    The story is split into atomic claims: what is asserted, about whom, over what dates, supported by what.

  6. Corroboration

    Material disputed claims need at least two independent sources where feasible. An original official record is strong evidence of what that record itself states.

  7. Contradiction search

    We actively look for later orders, stays, reversals, acquittals, corrective action and alternative explanations.

  8. Right of reply

    Every material subject receives specific, fair questions. We record how and when notice was served and whether a response came.

  9. Pre-publication review

    An editor checks sourcing and wording; counsel reviews high-risk allegations; a fact-checker verifies amounts and dates; personal data is redacted.

  10. Publication and monitoring

    A named editor publishes the approved version. We monitor new orders and replies and update status with a visible change history.

"},{"type":"html","version":1,"html":"

Labelled money

Amounts are never blurred together.

AllegedAmount stated in a complaint or allegation; not established.
DocumentedAmount shown in a primary record we hold.
OrderedAmount directed by a court, regulator or authority.
RecoveredAmount confirmed as actually paid or recovered.
EstimateOur calculation; method stated alongside.
"},{"type":"html","version":1,"html":"

Scope

1 January 2011 to 2 November 2026, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. Some records link to earlier origins or later outcomes.

Jurisdiction is recorded as at the event date. Telangana became a separate state on 2 June 2014. Events before that date are recorded as undivided Andhra Pradesh, with the district and authority as they were at the time. We do not retroactively assign a pre-2014 event to a present-day state without checking.

Categories

Land ownership and land grabbingCompeting title claims, forged deeds, assigned-land transfer, government land occupation.
Builder and promoter misconductCollection before a compliant sale agreement, misrepresentation, duplicate sales, non-delivery.
Planning and approval irregularitiesUnauthorised layouts, construction deviations, missing permissions, encroachment.
Bribery and official corruptionAlleged payment demands, trap cases, approvals allegedly influenced by undue advantage.
Undisclosed or suspicious property moneyUndervaluation, benami allegations, laundering links, shell-company ownership.
Government land allotment and public assetsConcessional allotment, non-use, change of purpose, unmet conditions.
Buyer harm and project failureDelayed possession, refund disputes, hidden charges, missing amenities.
Institutional failureComplaints not acted upon, repeated permissions despite known violations.

Language we avoid

We do not label a transaction “black money”, a person “corrupt” or a company a “scam” unless the evidence and legal status justify exactly that wording. We publish no rankings or scores of people.

"}],"direction":"ltr","format":"","indent":0,"type":"root","version":1}}

  • Substantiated factual errors are corrected promptly and visibly on the record itself.
  • Status updates (new orders, appeals, stays) are recorded with the date and source.
  • A record is withdrawn only with a public withdrawal notice and an editor’s recorded rationale.
  • Previous versions are kept in the editorial revision history.

posts.title: Right of reply
posts.lexical:
{"root":{"children":[{"type":"html","version":1,"html":"

Before publication

  1. We identify every subject

    Company, promoter, official, department, contractor or other named party in a material claim.

  2. We send specific questions

    A neutral summary of each claim concerning you, with dates and enough detail for a meaningful answer.

  3. We give a reasonable deadline

    Proportionate to the story. We keep proof of delivery and follow-up attempts.

  4. We publish your response fairly

    Including denials, explanations and documents. We do not paraphrase a denial to weaken it.

  5. Silence is not an admission

    If there is no response, we say when and how we asked — and nothing more.

"},{"type":"html","version":1,"html":"

After publication

If you are named in a record, or you believe something is wrong, write to the editor with the record ID shown at the top of the record, the specific statement and any document that shows it is inaccurate or out of date.

\n

Contact channel — being set up

A dedicated corrections address will be published here before the first real record goes live. Every request is logged and answered, and any resulting change appears on the corrections page.

"}],"direction":"ltr","format":"","indent":0,"type":"root","version":1}}
posts.custom_excerpt: Anyone named in a record is asked specific questions before publication, and can respond or request a correction afterwards.

posts.title: Funding & independence
posts.lexical:
{"root":{"children":[{"children":[{"detail":0,"format":0,"mode":"normal","style":"","text":"Editorial independence","type":"extended-text","version":1}],"direction":"ltr","format":"","indent":0,"type":"extended-heading","version":1,"tag":"h2"},{"type":"html","version":1,"html":"
  • No developer, broker, political party, official or complainant can pay to add, suppress, remove or alter a case.
  • Sponsorship, advertising and donations are kept separate from case selection and editorial decisions.
  • Political and commercial affiliations play no part in which cases we investigate.
  • Serious allegations follow a two-person rule: one researcher builds the case; a second editor independently checks each material claim.
  • Corrections are public and versioned.

Intake is not open yet

We will accept reports only after an independent security review and legal sign-off on how submissions are stored, who can see them and how long they are kept. The form below shows what intake will ask for; it cannot be submitted.

Before you share anything

We cannot promise absolute anonymity. When intake opens, this page will explain exactly what the channel records (for example IP addresses or email headers), who on the team can see your identity, and when we might be legally compelled to share information.

Your identity will be stored separately from any case record. Case editors will not see it by default.

Never send us

  • Aadhaar or PAN numbers
  • Full bank account or card numbers
  • Passwords or login details
  • Unrelated family information
  • Material obtained by trespass, hacking or unlawful recording
What happened
Contact (optional)

File upload will be added only after malware scanning, quarantine storage and encryption are in place.
